news.headline: Madhya Pradesh Forest Department seeks approval to relocate cheetahs to Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve
news.story_lead: The Madhya Pradesh forest department has approached the National Tiger Conservation Authority for permission to shift cheetahs into the Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve, marking the first time the big cats will inhabit tiger territory in India. This move will make the reserve the third home for cheetahs in the state alongside Kuno National Park and Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary.
news.full_article_text:
The Madhya Pradesh forest department has initiated steps to introduce cheetahs into the Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve (VDTR), setting the stage for an unprecedented co-existence between cheetahs and tigers in the wild. According to L Krishnamurthy, additional principal chief conservator of forest (APCCF) for wildlife, formal permission has been sought from the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA). 

Currently, Madhya Pradesh houses 60 cheetahs in total. Among these, 57 are located at Kuno National Park—where the initial batch of African cheetahs was translocated four years ago—and three are housed at the Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary. VDTR will serve as the third designated home for the species in the state. Spanning an area of 2,300 square kilometres, VDTR currently accommodates around 30 tigers and will also provide the first rocky terrain habitat for cheetahs in India.

Wildlife experts and conservationists hold varied perspectives on this ecological experiment. A South Africa cheetah expert noted that tigers and cheetahs coexist in private reserves in South Africa but not in the wild, describing the move as a valuable learning experience for cheetahs to share space with leopards and tigers. Susan E Yannetti of the Metapopulation Initiative pointed out that cheetahs and tigers last shared a habitat in significant numbers in India about a century ago, and suggested that a cheetah's natural flight instinct would likely prompt it to run rather than fight when challenged. YV Jhala, former dean of the Wildlife Institute of India and leader of the initial translocation team, viewed the move positively, stating that while some cheetahs might initially be lost to tigers, adapting to coexist with other apex predators is essential for the project's expansion. He also emphasised moving away from bomas and allowing free-ranging cheetahs in restored habitats.

VDTR field director Rajneesh Singh highlighted historical evidence of coexistence, noting that Asiatic cheetahs formerly shared space with tigers and leopards. He pointed out that their prey bases differ significantly, with cheetahs hunting baby nilgais, deer, chitals, and blackbucks, while tigers face no such dietary limitations. Furthermore, because cheetahs prefer open grasslands and tigers lean toward dense forests across a vast reserve area, the probability of conflict remains low. Preparations at VDTR include two bomas for initial housing, alongside four quarantine compartments and five soft-release enclosures spread across 439 hectares.
news.background_context: African cheetahs were first translocated to India in September 2022, comprising eight cheetahs from Namibia, 12 from South Africa, and nine from Botswana.

Evaluating the ecological viability of co-existence between cheetahs, leopards, and tigers provides important insights into carnivore conservation, habitat management, and prey-base segregation.

hindi_translation.story_lead: मध्य प्रदेश वन विभाग ने वीरांगना दुर्गावती टाइगर रिजर्व में चीतों को स्थानांतरित करने के लिए राष्ट्रीय बाघ संरक्षण प्राधिकरण से अनुमति मांगी है, जिससे यह भारत में चीता और बाघ के सह-अस्तित्व का पहला प्रयास बन जाएगा।

news.headline: TIPRA Motha secures massive victory in Tripura's TTAADC village council elections
news.story_lead: The TIPRA Motha party, an alliance partner of the ruling BJP in Tripura, has won over 2,600 seats in the Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC) village council elections. The results, declared on Monday, saw voting conducted across 2,950 seats while thousands of other positions were decided unopposed following Supreme Court directives.
news.full_article_text:
The TIPRA Motha party, ruling BJP ally in Tripura, secured a decisive victory by winning 2,670 seats in the Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC) village council elections, the results of which were declared on Monday. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) secured 470 seats, while its other ally, the Indigenous People's Front of Tripura (IPFT), won 16 seats. Independent candidates bagged 83 seats, whereas opposition parties CPIM and Congress won 38 and 10 seats respectively, having contested independently.

Out of 4,597 total seats scheduled for polls across 587 village committees, actual voting took place in 2,950 seats. As many as 1,644 seats were won unopposed, which included 1,561 secured by the TIPRA Motha party, 81 by the BJP, and one each by the CPIM and an independent candidate. The elections were conducted following a directive from the Supreme Court to the state Election Commission, acting on a petition filed by TIPRA Motha chief Pradyot Kishore Debbarma to hold the polls by the first week of September.

The five-year term of the elected village committees had originally concluded in 2021, but elections were delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Vote counting commenced at 8 AM, though tensions emerged in several areas, including protests and road blockades in the Sepahijala and Dhalai districts. Security forces also resorted to a lathi charge following a confrontation outside a counting centre in the Tulasikhar block of Khowai district.

Reacting to the outcome, TIPRA Motha chief Pradyot Bikram Kishore Manikya Debbarma stated that the mandate restores grassroots power to the people and reflects the culmination of his legal struggle in the Supreme Court to safeguard constitutional rights. Earlier this April, the TIPRA Motha party had also triumphed in the 28-seat TTAADC polls by winning 24 seats, while the BJP's tally dropped from eight seats in the previous council elections to just four.
news.background_context: The five-year term of the elected village committees expired in 2021 but could not be conducted due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The Supreme Court had previously directed the state Election Commission to hold the village council polls by the first week of September following a petition by TIPRA Motha supremo Pradyot Kishore Debbarma.

hindi_translation.headline: त्रिपुरा: TIPRA मोथा ने TTAADC ग्राम परिषद चुनावों में 2000 से अधिक सीटें जीतीं
hindi_translation.story_lead: त्रिपुरा में सत्तारूढ़ भाजपा की सहयोगी पार्टी TIPRA मोथा ने त्रिपुरा जनजातीय क्षेत्र स्वायत्त जिला परिषद (TTAADC) के ग्राम परिषद चुनावों में 2,600 से अधिक सीटें जीत ली हैं। सोमवार को घोषित परिणामों के अनुसार, 2,950 सीटों पर मतदान हुआ जबकि सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के निर्देशों के बाद अन्य सीटें निर्विरोध जीती गईं।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
त्रिपुरा में सत्तारूढ़ भाजपा की सहयोगी पार्टी TIPRA मोथा ने त्रिपुरा जनजातीय क्षेत्र स्वायत्त जिला परिषद (TTAADC) के ग्राम परिषद चुनावों में 2,670 सीटें जीतकर शानदार जीत हासिल की है, जिसके परिणाम सोमवार को घोषित किए गए। भारतीय जनता पार्टी (भाजपा) ने 470 सीटें जीतीं, जबकि उसकी दूसरी सहयोगी पार्टी IPFT ने 16 सीटें हासिल कीं। निर्दलीय उम्मीदवारों ने 83 सीटें जीतीं, जबकि विपक्षी दलों CPIM और कांग्रेस ने स्वतंत्र रूप से चुनाव लड़ते हुए क्रमशः 38 और 10 सीटें हासिल कीं।

587 ग्राम समितियों के तहत 4,597 सीटों पर चुनाव होने थे, लेकिन वास्तविक मतदान 2,950 सीटों पर हुआ क्योंकि 1,644 सीटें निर्विरोध चुनी गईं, जिनमें TIPRA मोथा पार्टी से 1,561, भाजपा से 81 और CPIM तथा एक निर्दलीय से एक-एक सीट शामिल थी। TIPRA मोथा पार्टी प्रमुख प्रद्योत किशोर देबबर्मा द्वारा दायर एक याचिका के बाद सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने पहले राज्य चुनाव आयोग को सितंबर के पहले सप्ताह तक ग्राम परिषद चुनाव कराने का निर्देश दिया था।

चुनी गई ग्राम समितियों का पांच साल का कार्यकाल 2021 में समाप्त हो गया था, लेकिन कोविड-19 महामारी के कारण चुनाव नहीं हो सके थे। सुबह 8 बजे वोटों की गिनती शुरू हुई, हालांकि सिपाहीजाल और धलाई जिलों में विरोध प्रदर्शनों और सड़क जाम के साथ कुछ मतगणना केंद्रों पर तनाव बढ़ गया। खोवाई जिले के तुलासिकार ब्लॉक में एक मतगणना केंद्र के बाहर झड़प के बाद सुरक्षा बलों द्वारा लाठीचार्ज किए जाने से भी तनाव पैदा हो गया।

प्रतिक्रिया व्यक्त करते हुए, TIPRA मोथा पार्टी प्रमुख प्रद्योत बिक्रम किशोर माणिक्य देबबर्मा ने लिखा कि आज का परिणाम लोगों को जमीनी स्तर की शक्ति वापस दिलाएगा। अप्रैल में हुए 28 सीटों वाले TTAADC चुनावों में भी TIPRA मोथा ने 24 सीटें हासिल की थीं, जबकि भाजपा की सीटें पिछले जनजातीय परिषद चुनावों की तुलना में आधी रह गईं।

news.headline: Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee issues legal notice to SSKM Hospital over alleged medical report leak
news.story_lead: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee has served a legal notice to the authorities of the Institute of Post Graduate Medical Education & Research (IPGMER) in Kolkata. The notice demands an explanation regarding how her medical reports concerning a 2021 leg injury reached current Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. This development follows Adhikari's public release of a five-year-old medical document indicating no fracture or dislocation on Banerjee's leg.
news.full_article_text:
Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee has initiated legal action by serving a notice to the Institute of Post Graduate Medical Education & Research (IPGMER) authorities, commonly known as SSKM Hospital, in Kolkata. The legal notice seeks clarification on how confidential medical records pertaining to her leg injury, dating back to ahead of the 2021 state assembly elections, came into the possession of current Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. 

The legal step follows statements made by Adhikari, who claimed that Banerjee had faked her leg injury. To support his claim, Adhikari released a five-year-old medical record which allegedly stated there was no evidence of fracture or dislocation on Banerjee's leg. Arka Kumar Nag, counsel for Banerjee, dispatched the notice to Manimoy Bandyopadhyay, the director of IPGMER, along with two other senior hospital officials. The correspondence asks whether any medical records of Banerjee were placed before Adhikari, and if so, what due legal process was followed by the department of radio-diagnosis. Furthermore, the notice warns that if proper legal procedures were bypassed, the institution holds legal liability to initiate action against politically motivated officers involved in the data breach.

The controversy traces back to March 10, 2021, when Banerjee filed her nomination from the Nandigram assembly constituency, where she contested against her former aide-turned-rival Suvendu Adhikari. Hours after filing the nomination, she alleged she was attacked by unidentified men. Although the Trinamool Congress (TMC) eventually won the state assembly elections, Banerjee lost the Nandigram seat to Adhikari. Following the alleged attack, she claimed to have suffered a fractured leg, campaigning for the next two months on a wheelchair with a plastered left leg while a Criminal Investigation Department (CID) probe was launched into the incident. Adhikari, citing findings from the department of radio-diagnosis at the Bangur Institute of Neuro-Sciences at IPGMER dated March 11, 2021, contended that medical findings showed no evidence of fracture or dislocation. Responding to the legal notice, Adhikari maintained that the documents were not obtained directly from SSKM hospital authorities and warned Banerjee against pushing the matter further, claiming he possesses additional X-ray plates and MRI reports.

The underlying incident dates back to March 10, 2021, when Banerjee alleged she was attacked by unidentified men after filing her nomination in Nandigram.
During the 2021 assembly elections, Banerjee campaigned on a wheelchair with a plastered leg, and a CID probe was initiated into the alleged attack.

Adhikari claimed the documents did not come from SSKM hospital authorities and warned that he could reveal further X-ray and MRI reports if pursued.

hindi_translation.headline: पश्चिम बंगाल की पूर्व सीएम ममता बनर्जी ने कथित मेडिकल रिपोर्ट लीक होने पर एसएसकेएम अस्पताल को नोटिस भेजा
hindi_translation.story_lead: पश्चिम बंगाल की पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री ममता बनर्जी ने कोलकाता स्थित इंस्टीट्यूट ऑफ पोस्ट ग्रेजुएट मेडिकल एजुकेशन एंड रिसर्च (IPGMER) के अधिकारियों को कानूनी नोटिस भेजा है। इस नोटिस में 2021 के विधानसभा चुनावों से पहले उनके पैर की चोट से जुड़े मेडिकल रिकॉर्ड मौजूदा सीएम सुवेंदु अधिकारी तक कैसे पहुंचे, इसका स्पष्टीकरण मांगा गया है। यह घटनाक्रम सुवेंदु अधिकारी द्वारा एक पांच साल पुरानी मेडिकल रिपोर्ट जारी करने के कुछ दिनों बाद सामने आया है, जिसमें कथित तौर पर ममता बनर्जी के पैर में किसी फ्रैक्चर या डिस्लोकेशन का प्रमाण न होने की बात कही गई थी।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
पश्चिम बंगाल की पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री ममता बनर्जी ने कोलकाता के एसएसकेएम अस्पताल (IPGMER) के अधिकारियों को एक कानूनी नोटिस जारी किया है। इस नोटिस के जरिए उन्होंने यह स्पष्टीकरण मांगा है कि 2021 के विधानसभा चुनावों से ठीक पहले उनके पैर की चोट से जुड़े गोपनीय मेडिकल रिकॉर्ड वर्तमान मुख्यमंत्री सुवेंदु अधिकारी के पास कैसे पहुंचे। यह कदम सुवेंदु अधिकारी के उस दावे के बाद उठाया गया है जिसमें उन्होंने कहा था कि ममता बनर्जी ने अपने पैर की चोट का नाटक किया था। अधिकारी ने एक पांच साल पुरानी मेडिकल रिपोर्ट सार्वजनिक की थी, जिसमें कथित तौर पर कहा गया था कि बनर्जी के पैर में कोई फ्रैक्चर या डिस्लोकेशन नहीं था।

ममता बनर्जी के वकील अर्का कुमार नाग द्वारा भेजे गए इस नोटिस में आईपीजीएमईआर के निदेशक मणइमोय बंद्योपाध्याय और अस्पताल के दो अन्य वरिष्ठ अधिकारियों से जवाब तलब किया गया है। नोटिस में पूछा गया है कि क्या क्लाइंट के मेडिकल रिकॉर्ड मुख्यमंत्री (अधिकारी) के समक्ष रखे गए थे, और यदि ऐसा था, तो रेडियो-डायग्नोसिस विभाग द्वारा कौन सी कानूनी प्रक्रिया अपनाई गई थी। नोटिस में चेतावनी दी गई है कि यदि कानूनी प्रक्रिया का पालन नहीं किया गया, तो अस्पताल प्रशासन की कानूनी जिम्मेदारी है कि वह इस सेंधमारी में शामिल अधिकारियों के खिलाफ आवश्यक कार्रवाई करे।

यह विवाद 10 मार्च 2021 का है, जब ममता बनर्जी ने नंदीग्राम सीट से नामांकन दाखिल करने के कुछ ही घंटों बाद अज्ञात लोगों द्वारा हमला किए जाने का आरोप लगाया था। हालांकि तृणमूल कांग्रेस (TMC) ने विधानसभा चुनाव जीत लिया, लेकिन ममता बनर्जी नंदीग्राम से सुवेंदु अधिकारी से चुनाव हार गईं। इसके बाद उन्होंने पैर में फ्रैक्चर का दावा किया और अगले दो महीनों तक प्लास्टर बंधे पैर के साथ व्हीलचेयर पर प्रचार किया। इस घटना की सीआईडी जांच भी शुरू की गई थी। सुवेंदु अधिकारी ने शनिवार को राज्य सचिवालय में संवाददाताओं से कहा कि 11 मार्च 2021 को आईपीजीएमईआर के बांगुर इंस्टीट्यूट ऑफ न्यूरो-साइंसेज के रेडियो-डायग्नोसिस विभाग के निष्कर्षों में स्पष्ट था कि पैर में कोई फ्रैक्चर या डिस्लोकेशन नहीं था।
bullet_points: पश्चिम बंगाल की पूर्व सीएम ममता बनर्जी ने कोलकाता के एसएसकेएम अस्पताल (IPGMER) के अधिकारियों को कानूनी नोटिस भेजा है।
नोटिस में पूछा गया है कि 2021 के उनके मेडिकल रिकॉर्ड मौजूदा सीएम सुवेंदु अधिकारी तक कैसे पहुंचे।
यह कार्रवाई सुवेंदु अधिकारी द्वारा एक मेडिकल रिपोर्ट सार्वजनिक किए जाने के बाद की गई है, जिसमें फ्रैक्चर न होने की बात थी।
नोटिस आईपीजीएमईआर के निदेशक मणइमोय बंद्योपाध्याय और दो अन्य वरिष्ठ अधिकारियों को वकील अर्का कुमार नाग के जरिए भेजा गया है।
विवादित मेडिकल रिकॉर्ड 11 मार्च 2021 के हैं, जो आईपीजीएमईआर के बांगुर इंस्टीट्यूट ऑफ न्यूरो-साइंसेज से जुड़े हैं।
घटना की शुरुआत 10 मार्च 2021 को नंदीग्राम में ममता बनर्जी द्वारा नामांकन के बाद कथित हमले के दावे से जुड़ी है।
चुनाव के दौरान बनर्जी ने व्हीलचेयर पर प्रचार किया था और मामले की सीआईडी जांच भी हुई थी।
2021 के चुनावों में सुवेंदु अधिकारी ने नंदीग्राम सीट पर ममता बनर्जी को हराया था।
key_facts: नोटिस पाने वाले: आईपीजीएमईआर (एसएसकेएम अस्पताल) के निदेशक मणइमोय बंद्योपाध्याय।
ममता बनर्जी के वकील: अर्का कुमार नाग।
विवादित मेडिकल रिपोर्ट की तारीख: 11 मार्च 2021।
प्रमुख राजनीतिक चेहरे: ममता बनर्जी और सुवेंदु अधिकारी।
important_dates: 10 मार्च 2021: ममता बनर्जी द्वारा नंदीग्राम में नामांकन और हमले का आरोप

news.headline: Prisons DIG M Somashekar Arrested in 2018 Life Convict Release Using Forged Supreme Court Order
news.story_lead: Deputy Inspector General of Prisons M Somashekar has been arrested for his alleged involvement in using a fabricated Supreme Court order to facilitate the release of a life convict in 2018. Somashekar, who served as the chief superintendent of Parappana Agrahara Central Prison at the time, was remanded to five days in police custody by an ACMM court.
news.full_article_text:
Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Prisons M Somashekar was arrested on Sunday night in connection with the illegal release of a life convict from Parappana Agrahara Central Prison in 2018. At the time of the incident, Somashekar functioned as the chief superintendent of the prison. On Monday, he was produced before a metropolitan magistrate (ACMM court) and subsequently remanded to five days in police custody as confirmed by Parappana Agrahara police inspector Naveen Kumar.

The case stems from the release of S Shankar on November 13, 2018, who walked free after jail authorities received paperwork purportedly issued by the Supreme Court of India. Investigators are currently scrutinizing how this fraudulent document was compiled, transmitted to the prison, and processed by staff before Shankar's discharge. Somashekar’s supervisory role during his tenure as chief superintendent is under detailed examination.

S Shankar had been serving a life sentence following his conviction in a murder and kidnapping for ransom case. Originally arrested in 2001, he faced charges under sections 364A and 120B of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). Upon conviction, the court had ordered his sentences to run concurrently.

Prior to Somashekar's arrest, law enforcement authorities apprehended Shankar himself alongside S Srikanth, a former second division assistant at the same prison. Investigators suspect that Srikanth played a central role in drafting the forged Supreme Court document. Police are tracking every phase of the conspiracy, from the creation of the fake order to its ultimate execution, reviewing relevant administrative records and evidence to determine the full chain of complicity among prison personnel currently serving or active at the time.
bullet_points: DIG M Somashekar was arrested on Sunday night over the 2018 release of a life convict using a fake Supreme Court order.
At the time of the incident in 2018, Somashekar was the chief superintendent of Parappana Agrahara Central Prison.
The accused police officer was produced before an ACMM court on Monday and remanded to five days in police custody.
The life convict, S Shankar, walked out of prison on November 13, 2018, after authorities processed a fraudulent document purporting to be from the Supreme Court.
Shankar had been serving a life sentence after being arrested in 2001 for murder and kidnapping for ransom under sections 364A and 120B of the IPC.
Police have also arrested S Srikanth, a former second division assistant at the prison suspected of drafting the fake Supreme Court document.
Somashekar is currently posted as a DIG in the Prisons Department in Kalburgi.
key_facts: DIG M Somashekar was the chief superintendent of Parappana Agrahara Central Prison in 2018.
Life convict S Shankar was freed on November 13, 2018, based on a forged Supreme Court order.
S Shankar was originally arrested in 2001 for murder and kidnapping for ransom under IPC sections 364A and 120B.
S Srikanth, a former second division assistant at the prison, was arrested on suspicion of fabricating the fake Supreme Court order.
Somashekar was remanded to five days in police custody following his production before an ACMM court.

November 13, 2018: S Shankar was released from prison using a forged Supreme Court order.

Cases of this nature highlight the urgent need for robust institutional protocols, digital tracking of judicial communications, and stringent internal vigilance to prevent corruption and safeguard the rule of law.

government_steps: Police investigation into the conspiracy involving prison officials and administrative staff.

It underscores the necessity of strict electronic verification protocols for judicial warrants, enhanced accountability for prison superintendents, and rigorous internal oversight to curb corruption within correctional institutions.

hindi_translation.headline: 2018 में आजीवन कारावास के कैदी को रिहा करने के लिए फर्जी सुप्रीम कोर्ट आदेश का उपयोग करने के मामले में जेल डीआईजी सोमशेखर गिरफ्तार
hindi_translation.story_lead: जेल उप महानिरीक्षक (DIG) एम. सोमशेखर को 2018 में एक आजीवन कारावास के कैदी को रिहा करने के लिए कथित तौर पर जाली सुप्रीम कोर्ट के आदेश का उपयोग करने के आरोप में गिरफ्तार किया गया है। घटना के समय सोमशेखर परप्पाना अग्रहारा केंद्रीय कारागार के मुख्य अधीक्षक थे।
hindi_translation.full_article_text: जेल उप महानिरीक्षक (DIG) एम. सोमशेखर को रविवार रात को गिरफ्तार कर लिया गया। उन पर वर्ष 2018 में परप्पाना अग्रहारा केंद्रीय कारागार से एक आजीवन कारावास के कैदी को मुक्त करने के लिए कथित रूप से जाली उच्चतम न्यायालय के आदेश का उपयोग करने का आरोप है। घटना के समय सोमशेखर इसी जेल के मुख्य अधीक्षक थे। परप्पाना अग्रहारा पुलिस निरीक्षक नवीन कुमार के अनुसार, सोमशेखर को सोमवार को एसीएमएम अदालत के समक्ष पेश किया गया, जहां से उन्हें पांच दिन की पुलिस हिरासत में भेज दिया गया। यह मामला 13 नवंबर 2018 को एस. शंकर की रिहाई के बाद सामने आया, जो जेल अधिकारियों को उच्चतम न्यायालय से रिहाई का आदेश मिलने के बाद जेल से बाहर निकल गया था। पुलिस इस बात की जांच कर रही है कि दस्तावेज कैसे तैयार किया गया, जेल तक कैसे पहुंचा और शंकर की रिहाई से पहले इसकी जांच कैसे की गई। पुलिस उस समय जेल के मुख्य अधीक्षक के रूप में सोमशेखर की भूमिका की भी जांच कर रही है। शंकर को 2001 में एक हत्या और फिरौती के लिए अपहरण के मामले में गिरफ्तार किया गया था और भारतीय दंड संहिता (IPC) की धारा 364A तथा 120B के तहत मामला दर्ज किया गया था। बाद में उसे दोषी ठहराया गया और आजीवन कारावास की सजा सुनाई गई। पुलिस पहले ही शंकर और परप्पाना अग्रहारा केंद्रीय कारागार के पूर्व द्वितीय श्रेणी सहायक एस. श्रीकांत को गिरफ्तार कर चुकी है। जांचकर्ताओं को संदेह है कि श्रीकांत ने ही जाली उच्चतम न्यायालय का दस्तावेज तैयार किया था। पुलिस यह पता लगाने का प्रयास कर रही है कि फर्जी आदेश तैयार होने और शंकर की रिहाई के बीच क्या-क्या हुआ। सोमशेखर वर्तमान में कलबुर्गी में जेल विभाग में डीआईजी के रूप में कार्यरत हैं।
bullet_points: जेल डीआईजी एम. सोमशेखर को रविवार रात 2018 में फर्जी सुप्रीम कोर्ट आदेश के जरिए कैदी को रिहा करने के मामले में गिरफ्तार किया गया।
2018 में घटना के समय सोमशेखर परप्पाना अग्रहारा केंद्रीय जेल के मुख्य अधीक्षक थे।
सोमवार को उन्हें एसीएमएम अदालत में पेश किया गया और पांच दिन की पुलिस हिरासत में भेजा गया।
आजीवन कैदी एस. शंकर 13 नवंबर 2018 को फर्जी सुप्रीम कोर्ट दस्तावेज के आधार पर जेल से बाहर आया था।
शंकर को 2001 में आईपीसी की धारा 364A और 120B के तहत गिरफ्तार किया गया था।
जेल के पूर्व सहायक एस. श्रीकांत को फर्जी दस्तावेज तैयार करने के संदेह में गिरफ्तार किया गया है।
key_facts: एम. सोमशेखर 2018 में परप्पाना अग्रहारा केंद्रीय जेल के मुख्य अधीक्षक थे।
कैदी एस. शंकर को 13 नवंबर 2018 को फर्जी सुप्रीम कोर्ट आदेश पर रिहा किया गया था।
एस. श्रीकांत को फर्जी दस्तावेज बनाने के संदेह में गिरफ्तार किया गया है।
important_dates: 2001: एस. शंकर की गिरफ्तारी।
13 नवंबर 2018: फर्जी आदेश पर एस. शंकर की जेल से रिहाई।
अक्टूबर 2026: डीआईजी एम. सोमशेखर की गिरफ्तारी।

news.headline: Former Civil Servants and Activists Serve Impeachment Notice Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
news.story_lead: A delegation of former bureaucrats and social activists has submitted a chargesheet and impeachment notice against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of proved misbehaviour under Article 324(5) of the Constitution. The notice lists six specific charges ranging from unauthorized changes to electoral forms to mass disenfranchisement through the Special Intensive Revision.
news.full_article_text:
A delegation comprising former civil servants and social activists submitted a formal chargesheet and notice of impeachment against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, demanding his removal from office. The action was taken invoking Article 324(5) of the Constitution of India, with the delegation accusing Kumar of a sustained pattern of wilful disregard of law, constitutional duty, and abuse of authority. The development occurred amidst reported police barricading around routes leading to the Election Commission of India (ECI) headquarters.

The chargesheet outlines six distinct allegations against the CEC. First, the delegation accused Kumar of undermining the collective functioning of the ECI by making decisions without adequate consideration by the full commission, specifically pointing to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and alleged objections raised by two other Election Commissioners. Second, it alleged unauthorized and illegal changes to Form 6, which is used for including names in electoral rolls, requiring existing voters to declare themselves as first-time applicants. Third, it questioned the unlawful deployment of ECINET, which purportedly bypassed statutory Electoral Registration Officers. Fourth, it characterized the SIR exercise as mass disenfranchisement, claiming that 13.3 crore names had already been deleted and projecting that the adult-to-electorate gap could reach 15 crore or more, disproportionately affecting vulnerable sections including women, the poor, migrants, minorities, and the elderly.

The fifth charge centered on conduct affecting the ECI's impartiality, citing public interventions involving opposition leaders and combative rhetoric that created perceptions of political alignment. Finally, the sixth charge invoked Section 32(1) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, alleging a wilful breach of statutory duty through altered forms, circumvention of officers, software usage, and concealment of records. Prominent signatories to the notice include former Delhi lieutenant governor Najeeb Jung, former home secretary G.K. Pillai, former secretary Amitabha Pandey, and several other retired bureaucrats and activists.
news.background_context: The notice invokes Article 324(5) of the Constitution regarding the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner and Section 32(1) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 concerning breach of statutory duty.
bullet_points: A delegation of former bureaucrats and activists moved an impeachment notice against CEC Gyanesh Kumar under Article 324(5) of the Constitution.
The chargesheet lists six specific allegations, including undermining the collective functioning of the ECI and unauthorized changes to Form 6.
The notice accuses the CEC of unlawful use of ECINET, which allegedly undermined the statutory authority of Electoral Registration Officers.
The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) was termed an exercise in mass disenfranchisement, with 13.3 crore names reportedly deleted.
Signatories to the notice include retired senior officials such as Najeeb Jung and G.K. Pillai, along with various social activists.
The delegation cited Section 32(1) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, alleging a wilful breach of official duty.

Constitutional provision invoked: Article 324(5)
Statutory provision invoked: Section 32(1) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950

Relevant for studying the institutional integrity, autonomy, and functioning of the Election Commission of India.
news.upsc_analysis: The development highlights intense public and civil society scrutiny over the administrative and procedural actions of India's election management body, focusing on constitutional checks, the independence of constitutional offices, and electoral roll management.
causes: Discontent among former civil servants and activists regarding administrative decisions and software implementations by the ECI.
impacts: Heightened debate over the autonomy, administrative transparency, and collective decision-making processes within the Election Commission of India.
challenges: Managing allegations of political partisanship and ensuring procedural transparency in large-scale electoral exercises like the Special Intensive Revision.

Section 32(1) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950
way_forward: Strengthening institutional transparency and fostering robust consultative mechanisms within election management bodies to preserve public trust.
news.mains_notes: The submission of an impeachment notice against the Chief Election Commissioner by former bureaucrats underscores vital questions concerning institutional autonomy, adherence to statutory duties, and collective functioning in constitutional bodies. Evaluating mechanisms under Article 324 is crucial for maintaining the democratic credibility of electoral processes.
mains_questions: Examine the constitutional provisions governing the removal of Election Commissioners and the significance of institutional autonomy in India's electoral democracy.
Discuss the challenges associated with electoral roll revisions and the role of consultative decision-making within the Election Commission of India.
news.takeaway: Former civil servants and activists served an impeachment notice against CEC Gyanesh Kumar under Article 324(5), listing six charges concerning ECI functioning and electoral roll revisions.

hindi_translation.story_lead: पूर्व सिविल सेवकों और सामाजिक कार्यकर्ताओं के एक प्रतिनिधिमंडल ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ 'सिद्ध कदाचार' का आरोप लगाते हुए एक चार्जशीट और महाभियोग नोटिस प्रस्तुत किया है, जिसमें संविधान के अनुच्छेद 324(5) के तहत उन्हें पद से हटाने की मांग की गई है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text: पूर्व सिविल सेवकों और सामाजिक कार्यकर्ताओं के एक प्रतिनिधिमंडल ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ औपचारिक रूप से चार्जशीट और महाभियोग नोटिस सौंपा और उन्हें पद से हटाने की मांग की। यह कदम भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 324(5) के तहत उठाया गया, जिसमें प्रतिनिधिमंडल ने उन पर कानून और संवैधानिक कर्तव्य की जानबूझकर उपेक्षा करने और अधिकार के दुरुपयोग का आरोप लगाया।
hindi_translation.background_context: यह नोटिस चुनाव आयुक्तों को हटाने से संबंधित संविधान के अनुच्छेद 324(5) और लोक प्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1950 की धारा 32(1) का हवाला देता है।
bullet_points: पूर्व नौकरशाहों और कार्यकर्ताओं के प्रतिनिधिमंडल ने अनुच्छेद 324(5) के तहत CEC ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ महाभियोग नोटिस दिया।
चार्जशीट में चुनाव आयोग के सामूहिक कामकाज को कमज़ोर करने और फॉर्म 6 में अनधिकृत बदलाव सहित छह आरोप शामिल हैं।
नोटिस में ECINET के गैरकानूनी उपयोग का आरोप लगाया गया है।
विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) को बड़े पैमाने पर मताधिकार से वंचित करने वाला अभ्यास बताया गया है।
नजीब जंग और जी.के. पिल्लई जैसे सेवानिवृत्त अधिकारी इस नोटिस के हस्ताक्षरकर्ताओं में शामिल हैं।

news.headline: Delhi Police Reject Assault Claims and Issue Media Guidelines Following ACP Promotion Amid Controversy
news.story_lead: The Delhi Police have dismissed allegations that female protesters were physically assaulted during a demonstration at Jantar Mantar as baseless while issuing new operational guidelines for journalists. The response follows controversy surrounding the promotion of Assistant Commissioner of Police Vivek Bhagat, who faces sexual harassment allegations from women journalists.
news.full_article_text:
The Delhi Police have rejected allegations of physical assault against female protesters during a demonstration in New Delhi as baseless and misleading. The clarification came from the Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) for New Delhi on social media, asserting that female protesters were handled exclusively by female staff and treated with dignity and due regard. The police added that all detentions and subsequent releases were executed strictly in accordance with applicable laws and prescribed procedures, noting that male protesters were similarly released within stipulated timeframes.

Controversy erupted following a protest on October 3, 2025/2026 against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar. During the demonstration, three women journalists alleged that police personnel subjected them to sexual harassment. One journalist specifically accused ACP Vivek Bhagat of assaulting and pushing her after she questioned him regarding the absence of women police personnel during protester detentions. In response to the backlash and following protests by independent journalists and social media influencers outside the Parliament Street police station, the complaints were transferred to the Crime Branch for an impartial inquiry.

Despite the ongoing inquiry, ACP Vivek Bhagat—previously serving in the Connaught Place area—was promoted to the rank of Additional DCP, alongside 11 other officers. Senior officials stated that the promotion was part of a routine order based on a proposal submitted earlier. The promotion drew severe public and political criticism. Organizations and figures such as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), founder Abhijeet Dipke, CJP member Ratna Singh, and human rights lawyer Vrinda Grover condemned the state action, arguing that it promotes impunity and could intimidate women from participating in public life.

Simultaneously, the Delhi Police issued official guidelines for journalists covering public protests. The advisory mandates that media personnel carry valid organization-issued identification cards or valid Press Information Bureau (PIB) or Delhi Information and Publicity (DIP) accreditation cards. Journalists are required to display their identification visibly at all times, ensure their activities do not obstruct police operations or law enforcement movement, and maintain a reasonable and safe distance during tense proceedings.
bullet_points: Delhi Police rejected physical assault claims regarding female protesters at a Jantar Mantar demonstration as baseless and misleading.
The controversy arose from an anti-CEC protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar held at Jantar Mantar on October 3.
Three women journalists accused police personnel of sexual harassment, with specific allegations leveled against ACP Vivek Bhagat.
ACP Vivek Bhagat was promoted to Additional DCP alongside 11 other officers, which police termed a routine order from an earlier proposal.
The complaints of sexual harassment have been transferred to the Delhi Police Crime Branch for a fair and impartial inquiry.
Independent journalists and influencers previously staged a protest outside Parliament Street police station demanding FIR registrations.
Human rights lawyer Vrinda Grover and the Cockroach Janta Party criticized the promotion as promoting state impunity.
Delhi Police issued new guidelines requiring journalists to display valid PIB, DIP, or organization ID cards and maintain a safe distance during protests.
key_facts: The protest took place at Jantar Mantar on October 3 against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
ACP Vivek Bhagat was promoted from ACP of Connaught Place area to Additional DCP.
Eleven other officers were promoted alongside ACP Bhagat in the routine order.
Investigations into the sexual harassment allegations were transferred to the Delhi Police Crime Branch.
New media guidelines require visibly displayed PIB, DIP, or organizational press identity cards.

Monday: Delhi Police issued clarifications, ACP Bhagat was promoted, and statements were released
exam_relevance: Useful for understanding police accountability, institutional procedures, and freedom of the press in India.
Highlights protocols for law enforcement during public demonstrations and media engagement.
news.upsc_analysis: The incident brings to light critical themes of police accountability, institutional transparency in handling misconduct allegations against law enforcement personnel, and the protection of press freedom during public demonstrations. It highlights the administrative challenges in balancing public order with individual rights.
causes: Allegations of sexual harassment and physical assault raised by women journalists during a protest at Jantar Mantar.
Public and political backlash regarding the promotion of an accused police officer during an active inquiry.
impacts: Transfer of harassment complaints to the Crime Branch for impartial inquiry.
Issuance of new operational and identification guidelines for journalists covering protests.
Widespread criticism from civil society, human rights activists, and political entities regarding state impunity.
challenges: Ensuring impartial investigation when accused personnel receive administrative promotions.
Maintaining trust between law enforcement agencies and media personnel covering tense public demonstrations.
government_steps: Transferring the sexual harassment complaints to the Crime Branch for inquiry.
Issuing formal guidelines and identification protocols for media persons covering protests.
Defending official procedures while maintaining that female protesters were handled by female staff with dignity.
way_forward: Ensuring transparent, time-bound, and independent investigations into allegations against law enforcement officers to uphold public trust and constitutional safeguards.
news.mains_notes: The controversy surrounding the promotion of a police officer facing sexual harassment allegations underscores institutional challenges in maintaining police accountability and protecting media freedom. While police authorities maintain that promotions follow routine administrative channels, civil society concerns point to the necessity of insulating inquiries from administrative decisions to prevent perceptions of impunity.
mains_questions: Discuss the challenges related to police accountability and institutional transparency in handling misconduct allegations against law enforcement personnel.
Examine the importance of safeguarding press freedom and establishing clear protocols for media personnel covering public demonstrations in India.
news.takeaway: Delhi Police rejected assault claims, transferred journalist harassment complaints to the Crime Branch, issued new media guidelines, and defended the routine promotion of ACP Vivek Bhagat amidst severe public criticism.
prelims_facts: The protest at Jantar Mantar targeted CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
Complaints of sexual harassment against police personnel were transferred to the Delhi Police Crime Branch.
New guidelines require journalists to carry PIB, DIP, or organization ID cards.

hindi_translation.headline: दिल्ली पुलिस ने मारपीट के दावों को खारिज किया, आरोपी एसीपी की पदोन्नति के बीच पत्रकारों के लिए दिशानिर्देश जारी किए
hindi_translation.story_lead: दिल्ली पुलिस ने जंतर-मंतर पर प्रदर्शन के दौरान महिला प्रदर्शनकारियों के साथ मारपीट के आरोपों को खारिज कर दिया है और पत्रकारों के लिए नए दिशानिर्देश जारी किए हैं। यह प्रतिक्रिया महिला पत्रकारों द्वारा यौन उत्पीड़न के आरोपी एसीपी विवेक भगत की पदोन्नति के बाद आई है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text: दिल्ली पुलिस ने नई दिल्ली में एक प्रदर्शन के दौरान महिला प्रदर्शनकारियों के साथ शारीरिक मारपीट के दावों को निराधार और भ्रामक बताया है। नई दिल्ली के पुलिस उपायुक्त (डीसीपी) ने सोशल मीडिया पर स्पष्ट किया कि महिला प्रदर्शनकारियों को महिला कर्मचारियों द्वारा संभाला गया था और उनके साथ उचित गरिमा के साथ व्यवहार किया गया था। पुलिस ने कहा कि हिरासत और रिहाई लागू कानूनों और निर्धारित प्रक्रियाओं के अनुसार की गई। यह विवाद 3 अक्टूबर को मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (सीईसी) ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ जंतर-मंतर पर हुए प्रदर्शन के दौरान तीन महिला पत्रकारों द्वारा पुलिसकर्मियों पर यौन उत्पीड़न के आरोप लगाने के बाद पैदा हुआ था। इस बीच, आरोपी एसीपी विवेक भगत को अतिरिक्त डीसीपी के रूप में पदोन्नति दी गई। पुलिस ने रविवार को घोषणा की थी कि शिकायतों को निष्पक्ष जांच के लिए क्राइम ब्रांच को ट्रांसफर कर दिया गया है। इसके साथ ही दिल्ली पुलिस ने विरोध प्रदर्शनों को कवर करने वाले पत्रकारों के लिए मान्यता प्राप्त पहचान पत्र दिखाने और उचित दूरी बनाए रखने से जुड़े नए दिशानिर्देश भी जारी किए हैं।
bullet_points: दिल्ली पुलिस ने जंतर-मंतर पर महिला प्रदर्शनकारियों के साथ मारपीट के आरोपों को निराधार बताया।
यह विवाद 3 अक्टूबर को सीईसी ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ हुए विरोध प्रदर्शन के दौरान सामने आया।
तीन महिला पत्रकारों ने पुलिसकर्मियों पर यौन उत्पीड़न का आरोप लगाया, जिसमें एसीपी विवेक भगत का नाम शामिल है।
आरोपी एसीपी विवेक भगत को अतिरिक्त डीसीपी के रूप में पदोन्नति दी गई।
शिकायतों को निष्पक्ष जांच के लिए क्राइम ब्रांच को स्थानांतरित कर दिया गया है।
दिल्ली पुलिस ने पत्रकारों के लिए पीआईबी, डीआईपी या संस्थागत पहचान पत्र दिखाना अनिवार्य करते हुए नए दिशानिर्देश जारी किए।
key_facts: विरोध प्रदर्शन 3 अक्टूबर को जंतर-मंतर पर आयोजित किया गया था।
एसीपी विवेक भगत को अतिरिक्त डीसीपी पद पर पदोन्नत किया गया।
यौन उत्पीड़न के मामलों की जांच क्राइम ब्रांच को सौंपी गई है।
important_dates: 3 अक्टूबर: जंतर-मंतर पर विरोध प्रदर्शन और घटना

news.headline: Telangana Tea Vendor Sets Himself Ablaze Near Police Station in Nizamabad District
news.story_lead: A 55-year-old tea stall owner attempted suicide by setting himself on fire within the premises of a police station in Telangana's Nizamabad district. While authorities attributed the extreme step to a local business dispute and a petty case regarding late-night operations, local residents and activists staged protests demanding action against a Sub-Inspector.
news.full_article_text: A 55-year-old tea vendor took the extreme step of setting himself on fire outside a police station in Bheemgal town, located in Telangana's Nizamabad district. Carrying a bottle of petrol and a matchbox, the middle-aged man walked into the police station premises on Monday morning and poured fuel on himself before igniting it. Present police personnel and bystanders quickly intervened, extinguished the flames, and rushed him to a hospital for medical treatment. According to police statements, the vendor was under distress following a rivalry with a local grocery shop owner. The tea seller had recently stopped purchasing cigarettes and other inventory from the grocery store, which allegedly prompted the grocer to send two local reporters to intimidate him. Additionally, the police had booked a petty case against the vendor for operating his tea stall during late-night hours as part of routine enforcement. A Sub-Inspector had instructed him to pay the fine through the court. Nizamabad Police Commissioner P Sai Chaitanya maintained that the police bore no fault in the matter. Meanwhile, local residents and political activists organized demonstrations in Bheemgal town, demanding disciplinary action against the Sub-Inspector who issued the petty case.
bullet_points: A 55-year-old tea stall owner attempted suicide by self-immolation outside a police station in Telangana.
The incident occurred on Monday morning in Bheemgal town of Nizamabad district.
The man walked to the police station carrying a bottle of petrol and a matchbox before setting himself ablaze.
Police personnel and bystanders intervened promptly, doused the flames, and hospitalized the victim.
Authorities stated that the vendor was distressed over a rivalry with a grocery shop owner who allegedly sent reporters to threaten him.
The tea seller had stopped buying cigarettes and supplies from the particular grocery shop.
Police had registered a petty case against the vendor for running his shop during late-night hours and asked him to pay a court fine.
Nizamabad Police Commissioner P Sai Chaitanya stated there was no fault on the part of the police.
Local residents and political activists staged protests demanding action against the concerned Sub-Inspector.
key_facts: Victim: 55-year-old tea stall owner
Location: Bheemgal town, Nizamabad district, Telangana
Date of incident: Monday
Nizamabad Police Commissioner: P Sai Chaitanya
Triggers cited by police: Business dispute over cigarette/material purchase and a petty case for late-night operation
important_dates: Monday - The day the tea seller attempted self-immolation at the police station
exam_relevance: Relevant for General Studies (GS Paper II) focusing on police accountability, police-public relations, grievance redressal mechanisms, and administrative ethics in India.
news.upsc_analysis: This incident highlights local friction points involving routine police enforcement, informal local disputes, and public trust in law enforcement agencies. It underscores the importance of sensitive handling of petty offences by local police and effective grievance redressal mechanisms to prevent extreme public reactions.
causes: Dispute with a local grocery shop owner over stopping the purchase of cigarettes and supplies
Intimidation by individuals allegedly sent by the grocer
Registration of a petty case by police for running the tea shop during late-night hours
impacts: Severe burn injuries to the 55-year-old tea vendor requiring hospitalization
Protests by local residents and political activists demanding action against the Sub-Inspector
challenges: Maintaining balanced and sensitive enforcement of petty municipal/police regulations without alienating local vendors
Addressing public grievances and ensuring transparency in police conduct
government_steps: Immediate intervention by police personnel and bystanders to extinguish the flames and hospitalize the victim
Public clarification by Nizamabad Police Commissioner regarding routine enforcement duties
way_forward: Sensitization of local police personnel in community policing and empathetic dispute resolution.
Strengthening institutional channels for informal grievance redressal to avoid escalation of petty commercial disputes.
news.mains_notes: The incident in Nizamabad, Telangana, where a tea vendor attempted self-immolation following local disputes and police action, brings to light structural concerns regarding police-public interface at the grassroots level. While routine enforcement of rules regarding operating hours is legally mandated, the manner of enforcement and handling of petty grievances require administrative sensitivity. Such episodes underscore the need for effective police reforms, empathetic policing, and accessible dispute-resolution mechanisms to bridge trust deficits between local authorities and citizens.
mains_questions: Discuss the challenges in police-public relations at the grassroots level in India and suggest measures to enhance sensitivity in routine law enforcement.
Examine the socio-economic vulnerabilities of informal sector vendors and the role of local administrative frameworks in addressing their grievances.
news.takeaway: A 55-year-old tea seller in Telangana's Nizamabad district attempted self-immolation outside a police station following a local business rivalry and a petty enforcement case, triggering local protests.
prelims_facts: Nizamabad district is located in the state of Telangana.
P Sai Chaitanya serves as the Nizamabad Police Commissioner.

hindi_translation.headline: तेलंगाना: चाय विक्रेता ने पुलिस स्टेशन के बाहर खुद को आग लगाई, पुलिस ने सिगरेट को लेकर हुए विवाद का दिया हवाला
hindi_translation.story_lead: तेलंगाना के निजामाबाद जिले में एक 55 वर्षीय चाय विक्रेता ने पुलिस स्टेशन परिसर में खुद को आग लगाकर आत्महत्या का प्रयास किया। पुलिस का कहना है कि वह दो स्थानीय संवाददाताओं द्वारा धमकी दिए जाने और किराना दुकान से जुड़े विवाद से परेशान था, जबकि स्थानीय लोगों और राजनीतिक कार्यकर्ताओं ने सब-इंस्पेक्टर के खिलाफ कार्रवाई की मांग को लेकर प्रदर्शन किया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text: तेलंगाना के निजामाबाद जिले के भीमगुल शहर में एक 55 वर्षीय चाय की दुकान के मालिक ने पुलिस स्टेशन परिसर में कथित तौर पर खुद को आग लगा ली। सोमवार सुबह यह व्यक्ति पेट्रोल की बोतल और माचिस लेकर थाने पहुंचा और खुद को आग के हवाले कर दिया। वहां मौजूद पुलिसकर्मियों और अन्य लोगों ने तुरंत आग बुझाई और उसे अस्पताल पहुंचाया। पुलिस के अनुसार, चाय विक्रेता एक किराना दुकान के मालिक के साथ कथित रंजिश के कारण तनाव में था। चाय विक्रेता ने हाल ही में किराना दुकान से सिगरेट और अन्य सामान खरीदना बंद कर दिया था, जिसके बाद किराना मालिक ने उसे डराने के लिए दो पत्रकारों को भेजा था। इसके अलावा, पुलिस ने देर रात तक दुकान चलाने के आरोप में उसके खिलाफ एक मामूली मामला दर्ज किया था और सब-इंस्पेक्टर ने उसे अदालत में जुर्माना भरने को कहा था। निजामाबाद के पुलिस कमिश्नर पी. साई चैतन्य ने कहा कि इस मामले में पुलिस की कोई गलती नहीं थी। इस बीच, भीमगुल शहर में स्थानीय लोगों और कार्यकर्ताओं ने सब-इंस्पेक्टर के खिलाफ कार्रवाई की मांग को लेकर प्रदर्शन किया।
bullet_points: तेलंगाना में एक 55 वर्षीय चाय विक्रेता ने पुलिस स्टेशन के बाहर आत्मदाह का प्रयास किया।
यह घटना सोमवार सुबह निजामाबाद जिले के भीमगुल शहर में हुई।
वह व्यक्ति पेट्रोल की बोतल और माचिस लेकर थाने पहुंचा था।
पुलिसकर्मियों और लोगों ने तुरंत आग बुझाई और उसे अस्पताल में भर्ती कराया।
पुलिस के अनुसार, वह एक किराना दुकानदार के साथ विवाद और धमकियों से परेशान था।
चाय विक्रेता ने उस किराना दुकान से सामान खरीदना बंद कर दिया था।
देर रात दुकान चलाने के लिए पुलिस ने उसके खिलाफ मामूली मामला दर्ज किया था।
निमाजाबाद पुलिस कमिश्नर पी. साई चैतन्य ने कहा कि पुलिस का कोई दोष नहीं था।
स्थानीय लोगों ने संबंधित सब-इंस्पेक्टर के खिलाफ कार्रवाई की मांग को लेकर प्रदर्शन किया।
key_facts: पीड़ित: 55 वर्षीय चाय विक्रेता
स्थान: भीमगुल शहर, निजामाबाद जिला, तेलंगाना
घटना का दिन: सोमवार
निजामाबाद पुलिस कमिश्नर: पी. साई चैतन्य
important_dates: सोमवार - जिस दिन चाय विक्रेता ने पुलिस स्टेशन के बाहर आत्मदाह का प्रयास किया
